Pipelines carry multiple fuels in batches; barges can transport several fuel types with multiple tanks; and the same railcar type is used for biofuels and petroleum products, but they are generally leased and used for a single product over the period of that lease. Dedicated trucks are used to move Jet A from terminals or refineries to airports where pipelines are not available. Figure 16. SAF and conventional jet fuel supply chains Jet fuel is commonly moved by pipeline, which is the preferred method to move transportation fuels due to efficiency and cost. Petroleum product pipelines were built to move fuel from refineries and import terminals throughout the country. Jet fuel may pass through one or more terminals before arriving at an airport. Pipelines batch fuels based on fuel properties, and if dissimilar fuels come into contact, a transmix or interface is delivered to a separate tank for reprocessing. Pipeline customers receive the specified volume of fuel; however, they are not receiving fuel from a particular terminal or refinery. For example, an energy company may ship their jet fuel on a pipeline to a terminal thousands of miles away and receive the volume of fuel ordered, but it is not necessarily the fuel from their refinery. While possible to track a segregated batch, it is both costly and uncommon; it has been done for demonstration purposes. For example, batches of Jet A/SAF blends from Houston terminals were sent up the Colonial Pipeline system and delivered by pipeline and truck to LaGuardia International Airport and Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport, respectively (Neste 2022; Business Air News 2025). 100% SAF (also referred to as neat SAF) has not been shipped on pipelines and would 22 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. require pipeline companies publishing rates per Federal Energy Regulatory Commission requirements. Barges are used to move fuels along rivers and inland waterways and along the costal United States. The federal Jones Act requires that all goods transported in U.S. waters be carried on U.S. vessels (U.S. Customs and Boarder Protection 2024). SAF has also been moved by tankers, ships designed for bulk transport of oil and petroleum products and generally move large volumes used for both imports and moving fuels within the United States. Jet A is not moved by rail. Biofuels, including ethanol and biodiesel, are commonly moved by rail due to both location of production and that neither are drop-in fuels. SAF has been moved by rail, primarily from the Montana Renewables plant to Southern California (BNSF Railway 2023). Not all terminals have rail facilities, and in those instances the biofuels are received at a transmodal facility and delivered to nearby terminals by truck. Trucks are used to move jet fuel from terminals to airports that do not have pipelines. Airports without fuel hydrant systems use trucks to move fuel to aircraft.
